title: Polynomial-time equality of binary values
statement: Let $f,g$ be polynomial-time computable functions from bit strings to bit strings. The Boolean-valued function that returns true exactly when the natural numbers represented by the little-endian outputs $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are equal, and otherwise returns false, is polynomial-time computable.
replaced: If two word producers are polynomial-time computable, then the single-bit test deciding whether their outputs denote equal natural numbers is polynomial-time computable, using the banked four-word comparator with the two remaining words empty.
